newsitem.title: UK: BA sees alliance boosting rivals by $1 bln.
newsitem.headline: BA sees alliance boosting rivals by $1 bln.

text.p: Bob Ayling, chief executive of British Airways Plc, said on Wednesday BA's alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines would allow its competitors to access a $1.0 billion slice of the pair's existing revenues.

Speaking at a London industry lunch, Ayling said that if the planned deal went ahead and met Britain's regulatory conditions on its approval -- namely the release of 168 weekly slots from London's Heathrow airport -- "competitors would be capable of earning $1.0 billion in revenues on these slots alone".
Ayling also predicted that services between Heathrow and the United States would grow by a fifth because of the slot move.
"This increase in services would be good for consumers, who would enjoy more choice, keener prices and better quality standards," a statement accompanying the speech added.
In his address to the UK Aviation Club, Ayling argued that BA believed it had been strengthened by strong competition from other British and foreign airlines.
"So, too, British Airway's success is not a threat to the rest of the European industry, but a means by which the whole industry can be strengthened," he said.

If the alliance is approved, BA added, the partners intend to launch at least one new service from the city of Manchester in northwest England to the United States, "and will also examine the possibilities of other new routes from Birmingham and Glasgow".
Looking at alliances in general, Ayling said that all European airlines would eventually have to face up to the challenge of becoming more competitive internationally.
This unavoidable logic had already led to three transatlantic alliances, he said, adding Air France was not expected "to remain a wallflower" for much longer.
